### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3230bdbf76844966623e21db5ac940e4b83fd1b9`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3230bdbf76844966623e21db5ac940e4b83fd1b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7f01128247a8fd1b5e35b52c183005b10c425e63` — the merge of head `e37497434c3983744185c320e40e5f698d1e3251` into base `3230bdbf76844966623e21db5ac940e4b83fd1b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 7f01128247a8fd1b5e35b52c183005b10c425e63 && git checkout 7f01128247a8fd1b5e35b52c183005b10c425e63
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3230bdbf76844966623e21db5ac940e4b83fd1b9 e37497434c3983744185c320e40e5f698d1e3251 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3230bdbf76844966623e21db5ac940e4b83fd1b9 && git merge --no-ff e37497434c3983744185c320e40e5f698d1e3251
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8660c53ef566e869a3da97d3afdac7f511e25b25`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/rls-membership-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.engine-judge.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/kernel-queue-membership.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/kernel-queue-membership.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-membership-keys.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-reserved-membership-keys.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object-membership-keys.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/ownership-queue-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Inputs read: card #27016 (body, claim 6458269562, amendment 6458307227, os-dev-report 6459486195), ruling 6457475657 and brief 6455628190 on #25769, PR #27044 body and file list (21 paths, equal to `git diff 7eb613c3..8660c53e`), the net diff, the cited code at the head, and the head's check-runs. Not the dispatch order and not the seat's conclusions.

Check-runs on the head at the time of this record: 47 total, 27 success, 8 skipped, 0 failure, 12 in progress — `Test Core (1/8)` to `(8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. Green already: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`. The verdict below stands on the diff and the cited code; the landing is Tier H (`skills/**`) and waits for the maintainer's hand and for the twelve running jobs regardless.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`queues` joins `RESERVED_RLS_MEMBERSHIP_KEYS`** (`rls-membership-resolver.ts`). Right: ruling 6457475657 letter A, verbatim. Every reader reads the list by import — `MembershipKeyNameSchema` (`rls.zod.ts`, the refine), `stageResolverMembership` and `RLSCompiler.userContextOf` (plugin-security), `membershipKeyReadsOf`, lint's `PRERESOLVED_USER_KEYS = new Set(RESERVED_RLS_MEMBERSHIP_KEYS)` — so no copy drifted. The three pins that count the list move with it: spec `object-membership-keys.test.ts` (`it.each` over the list, no edit), plugin-security `CELLS` (gains the `queues` cell), lint `KERNEL_KEY_RUNTIME_TYPE` (`queues: 'array'`).
2. **Accept-set narrowing at `ObjectSchema.membershipKeys`**: a key named `queues` is now refused at parse by the refine. Right, and this is the arm the amendment 6458307227 declared. Census re-run at the merge-base `7eb613c3` over `packages`, `examples`, `qa`, `skills`, `content`: 24 non-test files mention `membershipKeys`; none declares a key named `queues` (the only `queues:` lines are `stack.zod.ts`'s stack slot, not a membership key); no resolver lists `queues` in `keys`; no `rlsMembership` bag carries it. Zero movers — the body's claim holds.
3. **One producer, `kernel-queue-membership.ts`.** `stageKernelQueues` reads `host.ownershipQueueMembership()`, which `SecurityPlugin` resolves from the same `OWNERSHIP_QUEUE_SERVICE` slot `ownershipQueues()` (the claim gate's) resolves, and calls `queuesOf(userId, tenantId ?? null)`. In plugin-sharing's `OwnershipQueueService` both `queuesOf` and `isMember` go through `specsReachUser` with `newPass()` = `access` purpose, so a switched-off position confers nothing on either; the new plugin-sharing pin walks every (user, org, queue) of the fixture and is non-vacuous. Agreement with the claim gate holds for the same (user, queue, organization) triple. Right.
4. **Storage under a module-private symbol, bound to `(userId, tenantId)`.** `kernelQueuesOf` answers only when both match the context it is asked on; `{ ...ctx }` copies the symbol-keyed own property but a copy for another principal or organization answers `undefined`; the explain engine's delegator context (`explain-engine.ts`) is a fresh `buildContextForUser` object, so it resolves on its own. `context.queues` and `context.rlsMembership.queues` are never read: the compiler merge skips reserved names by name, and `userContextOf` takes `queues` from `kernelQueuesOf` alone. No leak across users or organizations found. Right.
5. **Fail closed.** No `userId` (the ADR-0138 guest principal is `principalKind: 'guest'` with no user id, so it is covered) → never resolved; no service → `resolveOnto` returns without staging; `queuesOf` throws → one WARN, not staged; a non-array answer → not staged; a frozen context → caught, not staged. Unresolved `current_user.queues` takes the compiler's existing unresolved-variable path → `deniedBy` → `RLS_DENY_FILTER`; a member of no queue gets `[]` → `empty-membership` → deny. Never all queues. Right.
6. **Lazy, once per request.** `policiesReadCurrentUserKey` walks the parsed CEL after `sqlPredicateToCel`, so the legacy `queue IN (current_user.queues)` spelling (the ADR's own) is detected too; both compile sites (`computeRlsFilter` at the `compilable` call, `computeWriteCheckFilter` at `withCheck`) pass their policies. `PENDING` is a `WeakMap` per context, so a settled or failed resolution is not retried on the same context. Right.
7. **Resolver screen.** `stageResolverMembership` drops a resolver's `queues` by name with the `RESERVED context key` WARN; the compiler merge is the second screen for a pre-seeded bag. Both are the existing screens, unchanged; adding the name to the list is what closes them. Right.
8. **No `ExecutionContextSchema` field.** The ruling says "the way it resolves `positions`"; `positions` is a schema field core writes at context assembly. The dev departed from that shape on purpose (a schema field is a forgeable string key; the service is a plugin service). Right — the lint's `kernelKeyProbe` binds a key with no declared field as an array, which is what the key holds, and the LISTS sentence in the explanation was reworded to stop claiming `ExecutionContext` declares every list key. Consistent.
9. **Lint.** `queues` becomes a kernel list key: `field in current_user.queues` stays accepted, `current_user.queues == x` now earns the type fault instead of the unknown-variable finding. The three `os explain` texts and the engine-judge pin list it; the `fix:` line's reword "Read a pre-resolved key" → "Read a kernel key" keeps the one-line bound (160 characters before the `suggestName` suffix, against 166) and matches the explanation's own vocabulary ("The kernel-resolved `current_user` keys"). Right.
10. **Published prose.** `rls.zod.ts` docblock, `ObjectSchema.membershipKeys` `.describe()`, and `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` list the kernel names with `queues`; the four `content/docs/references/**` pages are `gen:docs` output of those two spec edits (not reviewed; `check:generated` is CI's). The skill file's prose is accurate to the code: the refusal it teaches is the refine's.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/27016-queues-reserved-membership-key.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/skills` (`packages/skills`, published) at `minor`. Matches what the diff publishes: the kind is `narrowed`, so `minor` on every package the diff moves; `plugin-sharing` changes only a test, publishes nothing, needs no entry. Nothing extra. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body — `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — and agree with the amendment 6458307227. The title carries `!`, the body a `**BREAKING**` banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker in the gate's form, `not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`, a category `CATEGORIES` accepts, and the `**The remedy.**` line (rename the key; the new name is the author's). `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green on the head.

Clause-② read against the tree: the narrowing is real (the refine refuses the name) and the widening half is the platform's own value where before there was none, which the changeset states. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag (os-dev-report, out-of-scope 2): `current_user.queues` inside a field permission `when` resolves only if a row policy on the same context staged it; `compileRowPredicate` (`security-plugin-object-inputs.ts:397`) never stages. Answered: read in the tree, correct, and the outcome is the entry locking (fail closed), the same as declared membership keys since #25234. Not a widening and not this card's; no card owed from this record.
- Dev flag (out-of-scope 1): two `packaged-action-disabled-dispatch-live.dogfood.test.ts` failures on the dev's box, reproducing alone, in a stack nothing of which reads `current_user.queues`. Not this diff; the seat routes it. `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on the head.
- `open_questions`: none declared.
- Boundary noted, no fix on this head: the set is resolved for the ACTIVE organization (`tenantId`), as ADR-0142 D3 defines it and as plugin-sharing's `callerQueues` already reads it; the claim gate and `sitsInCallersQueue` ask membership in the ROW's organization (`queueOrganizationOf`). Under a group posture whose Layer 0 wall admits another organization's rows, a policy `queue in current_user.queues` would match that organization's rows carrying a same-named authored queue the caller does not sit in there. This is the ADR's definition and the pre-existing D3 read path, not something this PR introduces or could narrow alone; the authoring guide (execution-plan item 4) should say "active organization" in so many words.
- Boundary noted, fail closed: a context object whose `userId` or `tenantId` is changed in place AFTER staging answers `undefined` (identity mismatch) and is never re-resolved on that object (`PENDING` settled). No such in-place mutation exists in the tree after context assembly (`resolve-authz-context.ts` writes at build; the explain engine builds a fresh `dctx`).
- Escalation, should-fix outside this PR: ADR-0142 D3 on `main` still says "the queue service is the registered `IRlsMembershipResolver` for that one key" — option B's mechanism. The ruling chose A and this tree implements A. The decision record now names a mechanism the code does not use; a one-line amendment citing ruling 6457475657 is owed on a docs/adr PR (Tier H, outside this card's file surface). Not a defect of this head.
- Skills token ratchet: `security.md` measures 3687 tokens against its 3693 row (base: 3693 at zero headroom); the +3 of `, \`queues\`` was paid by deleting the clause "not a stamp on every data row," — a genuine deletion, not a re-wrap, and the lost clause is a second anti-pattern the roster sentence still implies. The row was not lowered; the script makes lowering optional ("may be lowered … encouraged"). `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is among the green runs that carry this gate.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`: before this PR the spec allowed any snake_case key not on the reserved list, so `membershipKeys: { queues: … }` and a resolver's `queues` were accepted, while ADR-0142 D3 already named `current_user.queues` as a platform-computed set. Reserving the name makes the spec's own refusal real — a declaration or resolver that could supply `queues` could seat any caller in any queue, which is exactly the "wall an app could redefine would not be a wall" reasoning the list already carries for `accessible_org_ids`. No declared capability is taken away at the consumer: the capability the ADR declares (a policy reads the caller's queues) is delivered on this head, and a key that could only ever have conflicted with it is withdrawn. Zero movers measured.

Tried to break it:
- Forge: `context.queues`, `context.rlsMembership.queues`, a resolver answering `queues`, a bag pre-seeded before the resolver runs — each path either never reads the name or drops it by name; the compiler merge is the choke point both faces pass. Held (and pinned in `kernel-queue-membership.test.ts` through the whole plugin's `getReadFilter`).
- Leak: a context copied for another principal (delegation) or organization — identity-bound answer, `undefined`. Held.
- Stale: the same context served twice in a request — resolved once; a membership change mid-request is not re-read, which is the same per-request semantics `positions`, `org_user_ids` and the resolver bag have. Acceptable.
- Fail open: no service, throwing service, no user, guest, non-array answer, frozen context — all unresolved → deny. Never a permissive filter. Held.
- Agreement with the claim gate: same service slot, same `specsReachUser` / `access` pass; differs only in which organization is asked, noted in ③ as the ADR's own definition.

Findings:
- must-fix: none.
- should-fix (follow-up, not this PR's surface): amend ADR-0142 D3's resolver sentence to the ruled mechanism (one kernel-side producer in plugin-security from the ownership-queue service), citing 6457475657.
- should-fix (optional, this file): lower the `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` ratchet row from 3693 to the measured 3687, the ratchet's ordinary direction.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-1d234m`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: PASS**

`Test Core (8/8)` failed on the previous head `8660c53e` in `@objectstack/rest`: one test, `src/data-nested-object-door.test.ts:288`, *"the cap: a condition matching more related records than the cap is REFUSED, never truncated; at the cap it is served whole"*, failed with `Test timed out in 5000ms` (1 failed / 6546 passed in the package).

Not this PR's:
- The test does not load `@objectstack/plugin-security`. It imports only `objectql`, `driver-sql`, `metadata-protocol` and the rest server. No file it reaches is in this diff.
- It passes locally on this branch (6 passed, 12 skipped).
- This is the known budget squeeze in #27004 (open): since #26930 a predicate delete walks the 1,001 matched rows one at a time, and this cap test's cleanup now nears its 5 s budget under CI load. No fix has landed yet, so there is nothing to port.

The new head `e37497434` (the two contract-review should-fixes) has a fresh CI run, and that run counts as this failure's one re-run.
